**B01AF03** is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for edoxaban, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) [^src3]. In the Danish healthcare system, this code is utilized to track and evaluate the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1]. 

Specifically, B01AF03 is a core component of the clinical quality indicators used to measure [[antikoagulationsbehandling]] (anticoagulation treatment) and the associated monitoring of renal function [^src1]. The code is listed alongside other primary anticoagulant therapies, including vitamin K antagonists ([[b01aa|B01AA]]) and other DOACs such as dabigatran ([[b01ae07|B01AE07]]), rivaroxaban ([[b01af01|B01AF01]]), and apixaban ([[b01af02|B01AF02]]) [^src1]. 

The documentation of B01AF03 appears in the national annual reports published by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP). These reports provide the technical definitions, inclusion criteria, and calculation rules necessary for standardizing data collection and comparing cardiovascular treatment quality across Danish regions [^src2] [^src3].
